berthing_information: 18 berths + 3 SPM + 1 Ro-Ro jetty; dedicated mechanized coal terminal (East Quay, 2 berths, 520m combined length, 15m alongside depth, capacity 20 MTPA, accommodates 60,000-75,000 DWT coal vessels); Capesize-capable berths at 16.5m draft / 300m LOA / 46m beam / 155,000 DWT (official PPA figure); approach channel depth 18.7m, entrance channel min depth 17.1m
coal_handling_capability: Yes - two dedicated mechanized coal berths (East Quay) commissioned 2001, 20 MTPA capacity, JSW Infrastructure redeveloping to 30 MTPA by design; also handles coking/steam coal at Central Quay and MPB berths (40-65,000 DWT range)
port_congestion_information: Qualitative only from public sources: port is a Major Port under GoI, high-traffic (~1,650 vessel calls/yr, ~46.4 million t/yr per one estimate; ~150.41 million t in FY2024-25 per Wikipedia/PPA data). No public daily congestion index found.
source: Paradip Port Authority (official website) + Wikipedia + WorldPortSource + ShipNext port profile

berthing_information: Two harbours: Outer Harbour (8 berths, LOA 390m / Beam 50m / Draft up to 18.10m, handles up to 200,000 DWT bulk/liquid cargo incl. coking & steam coal at VGCB - 356m quay, 3 ship loaders @2500 TPH each = 70,000 TPD); Inner Harbour (18 berths, LOA up to 230-240m / Draft 13-14.5m, Panamax-compatible, incl. Adani-operated EQ1 coal terminal, draft 14.5m, 27,000 TPD unload capacity)
coal_handling_capability: Yes - VGCB deep-draft berth (18.10m) for coking/steam coal up to 200,000 DWT; EQ1 mechanized coal terminal (Adani) at 14.5m draft for Panamax-class steam coal vessels
port_congestion_information: Qualitative only; no public daily congestion index found. Port handled record cargo volumes historically (68.01 million t in FY2010-11); more recent aggregate tonnage not verified in this research pass.
source: Visakhapatnam Port Authority (official documents/EIA reports) + Wikipedia + ShipNext

berthing_information: 9 berths total (1 iron ore, 1 coal, 3 multipurpose, plus Phase-II additions); 2 fully mechanized coal berths with combined 20 MTPA coal capacity; deepest all-weather port in India (harbor depth cited variously as 18-21m across sources, with 19.5-20.2m most consistently reported operational depth for cargo berths)
coal_handling_capability: Yes - two fully mechanized coal berths, 20 MTPA combined capacity; first Indian port to receive a fully-laden Capesize coal vessel (2009); designed for vessels up to 200,000 DWT
source: Global Energy Monitor (GEM.wiki) port profile + Wikipedia + Sea-Seek port directory

berthing_information: 3 multipurpose berths, 14.5m draft, 2.5km entrance channel; handles Handymax, Supramax and (mini-)Capesize class vessels; mechanized import berth for coal; owned/operated by Adani Ports & SEZ since March 2024 acquisition; natural harbor depth reported at 18.5m by some sources but 14.5m is the officially stated operational draft for berths
coal_handling_capability: Yes - mechanized coal import berth; described by Adani Ports as handling Handymax/Supramax/Capesize-class vessels within the stated 14.5m draft limit
source: Adani Ports official site (Gopalpur Port page + FY26 Operational Performance report) + Wikipedia

berthing_information: 6 operational berths (Phase 1: two 350m mechanized berths for coking/steam/thermal coal and limestone import, iron ore/steel export) plus rapid-loading silo (4,000 TPH capacity); 18km navigation channel supports 18m draft vessels; accommodates Super-Capesize, Panamax and Handymax vessels; current capacity ~40 MTPA (25 MTPA per some 2019-era sources), long-term master plan target of 100-314 MTPA
coal_handling_capability: Yes - core business is coking/steam/thermal coal import; rapid-loading silo (4,000 TPH); designed for Super-Capesize coal vessels at 18m draft
source: Adani Ports official site (Dhamra Port page) + Global Energy Monitor + Wikipedia + Adani press releases

berthing_information: Not a berthing port; functions as an outer/pilotage anchorage and transshipment/lightering point for Kolkata Port (Sagar pilotage station, ~45km downstream of Haldia; Sandheads is the outer pilot boarding ground at the mouth of the Hooghly). Used for ship-to-ship transloading (floating crane facilities commissioned Dec 2017; a 'baby Cape' vessel MV Kishore was handled at Sagar anchorage with 54,000t cargo) because deep-draft vessels cannot proceed up-river to Kolkata/Haldia.
coal_handling_capability: Used as a lightering/transloading anchorage for coal cargoes destined for Kolkata Port system; not a fixed-berth coal terminal
source: Kolkata Port Trust (Syama Prasad Mookerjee Port Authority) official pilotage page + IIFT working paper on Kolkata Port

berthing_information: Haldia Dock Complex (part of Syama Prasad Mookerjee Port, Kolkata): 12-17 berths (source-dependent count) inside an impounded dock entered via a single lock (built 1977); vessels restricted to LOA 240m / Beam 32.26m through the dock lock (236m LOA at some berths); oil jetties allow up to LOA 250m/Beam 44m; Wikipedia infobox lists max draft 9.1m, other port sources cite up to ~8.5-8.9m at Haldia Docks specifically, reflecting river siltation in the Hooghly; overall complex cargo capacity 46.70 MTPA (bulk, POL/crude, container)
coal_handling_capability: Limited - draft-constrained by Hooghly river siltation; larger coal parcels typically transloaded via daughter vessels/barges from Sagar/Sandheads anchorage rather than direct Capesize/Panamax berthing at Haldia itself
port_congestion_information: Pre-berthing delays at HDC reported to average ~2 days historically, with some vessels waiting over 5 days, attributed to single lock-gate entry system (per IIFT working paper) - qualitative, not a continuous daily index.
source: Kolkata Port Trust / Syama Prasad Mookerjee Port Authority official site + Wikipedia (Haldia Dock Complex) + IIFT working paper LD-22-58
